rotations.name: Rotation A — Chili Week

outputs.detail: Olive oil, dijon, red wine vinegar

steps.step: Start the rice cooker: 2½ cups dry brown rice. Preheat the grill or grill pan.
Chili base on the stove: brown 2 lbs of 93% lean turkey, add onion, garlic, cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika.
Into the chili pot: 2 cans black beans, 1 can kidney beans, 2 cans fire-roasted tomatoes, cup of broth. Lid on, low simmer — it needs nothing for an hour.
Season 2½ lbs of chicken breast (salt, pepper, garlic powder, smoked paprika) and grill in batches, about 6 minutes a side.
While chicken finishes: build 3 overnight-oats jars — ½ cup oats, 1 tbsp chia, ¾ cup Greek yogurt, splash of milk, berries on top. Fridge.
Vinaigrette jar: ¾ cup olive oil, ¼ cup red wine vinegar, big spoon of dijon, salt, pepper, shake. Lives in the fridge door all week.
Chop the week's vegetables: peppers, carrots, cucumbers into snack cups; slaw mix bagged; salad greens washed if needed.
Rice is done — fold in 3 cups of frozen cauliflower rice while it's hot (the steam cooks it). Portion into 5 containers.
Slice half the chicken for salads, cube the rest for bowls. Portion.
Kill the chili heat, stir in a squeeze of lime. Cool 20 minutes uncovered, then portion: 3 to the fridge, 2 to the freezer.
Label everything with the day it's for. Done — wash up while the chili cools.

rotations.weekPlan: Breakfasts: oats jars Mon–Wed, cook fresh Thu–Sun. Lunches: chicken over greens with the vinaigrette, chicken-rice bowls with salsa, or chili — zero cooking all week. Dinners: chili nights Mon and Wed, fresh-cooked the others (fish tacos and a stir fry both take 20 minutes when the rice is already made). Snacks: the hummus cups are already portioned.

rotations.name: Rotation B — Soup & Skillet Week

outputs.detail: Asian week needs its own sauce

steps.step: Oven to 425°. Slow cooker or covered pot on: 2 lbs chicken breast + a jar of salsa, low heat, walk away.
Lentil soup: sweat onion, carrot, celery, garlic in olive oil; add 2 cups green or brown lentils, cumin, a can of tomatoes, 8 cups broth. Simmer 45 minutes.
Sheet trays in the oven: peppers, broccoli, red onion, sweet potato chunks in olive oil, salt, pepper. 25–30 minutes, one stir.
Farro or brown rice on the stove — 2½ cups dry.
Jammy eggs: 6 eggs, 7 minutes in boiling water, straight to ice water, peel later while soup simmers.
Two dressings: the house vinaigrette, plus peanut-lime (3 tbsp peanut butter, lime juice, soy, water to thin, chili crisp).
Pull the roasted vegetables. Taste the soup, season, add a bag of spinach to wilt in.
Shred the salsa chicken with two forks right in the pot.
Portion everything: soup 3 fridge + 2 freezer, chicken, grains, vegetables into containers.
Label with days. Done.

rotations.weekPlan: Breakfasts: savory oats with a jammy egg on top (both already made), or the yogurt bowl. Lunches: lentil soup with Greek yogurt and hot sauce, or salsa chicken over grains with roasted vegetables. Dinners: salsa-chicken tacos on corn tortillas Monday, teriyaki salmon Tuesday (rice and vegetables already done — 15 minutes), Asian chopped salad with the peanut-lime dressing later in the week. Snacks: edamame from the freezer, the daily nuts.

rules: Fish never gets batch-cooked — it turns to cat food reheated. Batch the rice and vegetables so the fish itself is a 15-minute fresh cook.
Cool hot food uncovered for 20–30 minutes before lidding, and use shallow containers — deep tubs of warm chili are how food goes bad.
Fridge life is 4 days; anything for day 5 or later goes to the freezer the same night you cook it. Chili and soup freeze happily for 3 months.
Label with the day, not just the contents — a labeled fridge removes every decision from a Tuesday night.
Dressing in a jar means the salad takes 90 seconds; no jar, no salad. Make both dressings even if you're not sure you'll use them.
If the session runs long, cut the vegetable chopping, never the chili or soup — the pot dishes carry the most meals per minute of effort.
